063/**
064 * {@link org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.McpRevision} implementation for MCP revision {@code 2026-07-28}.
065 *
066 * <p>
067 * Owns this revision's stateless JSON-RPC method table, per-request {@code _meta} negotiation,
068 * SEP-2243 {@code Mcp-Method}/{@code Mcp-Name} header agreement checks, {@code server/discover}
069 * dispatch, and error-code table. Every request is independently negotiated from its own
070 * {@code _meta}; no handshake, session, or prior-request state exists.
071 *
072 * <p>
073 * <b>Constructed per binding, not shared as a singleton.</b> The bound servlet or mixin builds a
074 * fresh instance on every {@code revision()} call, passing its {@link McpOptions#getCapabilities()}
075 * result and its published {@link McpCacheConfig} into the constructor — see {@link McpRestServlet}
076 * and {@link McpEndpoint}. A {@code null} capabilities override auto-derives {@code server/discover}
077 * capabilities from the registered tool/prompt/resource/resource-template lists; a non-{@code null}
078 * override is advertised as-is. The cache config is binding-owned: it is supplied once at
079 * construction, is never {@code null}, and is treated as static and request-independent for the
080 * lifetime of this instance — every page of a given list method resolves to identical cache values.
081 * The instance retains no request-derived state.
082 */
083@SuppressWarnings({
084   // Settled, intentional name shadow against the neutral org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.McpRevision SPI
085   // (renaming this to e.g. AbstractMcpRevision was evaluated and rejected): every dated adapter binding
086   // class is deliberately de-versioned to plain "McpRevision" and differentiated from its siblings only by
087   // package, matching the revision-string-free naming already used throughout each vNNNNNNNN module.
088   "java:S2176"
089})

216   // 16 random bytes -> 22 base64url chars (unpadded): matches EphemeralKeyProvider's keyId minting pattern,
217   // sized generously since a jti only ever travels inside the AEAD-sealed plaintext, never on its own.
218   private static final int JTI_BYTES = 16;
219   private static final SecureRandom JTI_RANDOM = new SecureRandom();
220   private static final Base64.Encoder B64URL = Base64.getUrlEncoder().withoutPadding();
221   private static final Base64.Decoder B64URL_DECODER = Base64.getUrlDecoder();

223   // RFC 8785 canonicalizer for the argument hash, deliberately configured for UNBOUNDED depth with recursion
224   // detection: JcsSerializer's inherited depth-limit default of 100 SILENTLY truncates over-depth nodes to
225   // null, which would let two argument sets differing only below the limit hash identically while the handler
226   // still received the divergent subtree. Configuring an unbounded max-depth here makes the hash cover the
227   // full subtree, and enabling recursion detection fails fast, rather than looping, on a pathological cyclic
228   // structure. The complementary JSON value-safety check performed as part of the arguments-hash step is what
229   // actually bounds attacker-controlled depth, size, and CPU: this canonicalizer only guarantees that whatever
230   // passes that guard is hashed in full.
231   private static final Jcs JCS = new Jcs(
232      JcsSerializer.create().maxDepth(Integer.MAX_VALUE).detectRecursions().build(), JsonParser.DEFAULT);

256   @Override /* McpRevision */
257   public int errorCode(McpErrorKind kind) {
258      return switch (kind) {
259         case INVALID_REQUEST -> CODE_INVALID_REQUEST;
260         case UNKNOWN_METHOD -> CODE_METHOD_NOT_FOUND;
261         case TOOL_NOT_FOUND, PROMPT_NOT_FOUND, RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_PARAMS -> CODE_INVALID_PARAMS;
262         case INTERNAL_ERROR -> CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR;
263         case PARSE_ERROR -> CODE_PARSE_ERROR;
264      };
265   }

267   @Override /* McpRevision */
268   @SuppressWarnings({
269      "java:S3776" // Cognitive complexity acceptable for the single JSON-RPC dispatch entry point; splitting the notification/response/stream branching and the McpException/Exception recovery paths would fragment one cohesive request-to-result routine without real clarity gain.
270   })
271   public McpDispatchResult dispatch(McpExchange exchange, McpServerConfig config, BeanStore ctx) {
272      assertArgNotNull("exchange", exchange);
273      assertArgNotNull("config", config);
274      assertArgNotNull("ctx", ctx);
275
276      var req = exchange.request();
277      if (req == null)
278         return new McpResponseResult(reportError(ctx, null, errorCode(McpErrorKind.INVALID_REQUEST), "Request envelope is null"));
279
280      var id = req.getId();
281      var method = req.getMethod();
282
283      if (isEmpty(method))
284         return JsonRpcResponse.notification(id) ? null
285            : new McpResponseResult(reportError(ctx, id, errorCode(McpErrorKind.INVALID_REQUEST), "Missing method"));
286
287      // SEP-2350 per-operation step-up enforcement at the POST-parse point (method now known).  Deliberately OUTSIDE
288      // the try below: an insufficient-scope 403 (with its WWW-Authenticate step-up challenge) must propagate as a real
289      // HTTP 403 through the response processors, not be caught and folded into a JSON-RPC error over HTTP 200.
290      enforceStepUpScopes(method, req.getParams(), ctx);
291
292      try {
293         validateHeaders(exchange, req);
294         validateMeta(req.getParams());
295         if (McpMethods.SUBSCRIPTIONS_LISTEN.equals(method))
296            return JsonRpcResponse.notification(id) ? null
297               : new McpStreamResult(dispatchSubscriptionsListen(exchange, id, req.getParams(), config, ctx));
298         var result = finalizeResult(invoke(method, req.getParams(), config, ctx), config, ctx);
299         return JsonRpcResponse.notification(id) ? null : new McpResponseResult(JsonRpcResponse.ok(id, result));
300      } catch (McpException e) {
301         if (JsonRpcResponse.notification(id))
302            return null;
303         recordRpcError(ctx, e.getCode(), e.getMessage());
304         return new McpResponseResult(new JsonRpcResponse()
305            .setJsonrpc(McpProtocol.JSON_RPC_2_0)
306            .setId(id)
307            .setError(e.toJsonRpcError()));
308      } catch (Exception e) {
309         if (JsonRpcResponse.notification(id))
310            return null;
311         var message = e.getMessage() == null ? cns(e) : e.getMessage();
312         var code = errorCode(McpErrorKind.INTERNAL_ERROR);
313         recordRpcError(ctx, code, message);
314         return new McpResponseResult(JsonRpcResponse.errorResponse(id, code, message, JsonMap.of("type", cn(e))));
315      }
316   }

318   /**
319    * Enforces SEP-2350 per-operation step-up scopes for a dispatched request (the POST-parse enforcement point).
320    *
321    * <p>
322    * A no-op unless an {@link McpOptions} bean is bound and its {@link McpResourceServerConfig} is
323    * {@link McpResourceServerConfig#isEnabled() enabled} with a per-operation scope configured for this operation.  The
324    * MCP method &mdash; and thus the operation identity ({@link McpRoutingNames#routingName routing name}) &mdash; is
325    * known here (unlike the pre-parse {@code @RestStartCall} bearer gate), so a scoped {@code 403 insufficient_scope}
326    * step-up challenge naming exactly this operation's required scopes can be emitted.  Delegates the actual
327    * granted-vs-required comparison and challenge construction to {@link McpResourceServerSupport#enforceOperationScopes}.
328    *
329    * @param method The resolved JSON-RPC method.  Never <jk>null</jk>/empty at the call site.
330    * @param params The raw JSON-RPC request params (used to derive the operation name and passed through verbatim as
331    *    the {@link McpOperationContext#params() resolver seam}).
332    * @param ctx The per-request bean store (carries the bound {@link McpOptions} and {@link RestRequest}).
333    */
334   private static void enforceStepUpScopes(String method, Object params, BeanStore ctx) {
335      var opt = ctx.getBean(McpOptions.class).orElse(null);
336      if (opt == null)
337         return;
338      var cfg = opt.getResourceServer();
339      if (!cfg.isEnabled())
340         return;
341      var granted = McpResourceServerSupport.grantedScopes(
342         ctx.getBean(RestRequest.class).map(RestRequest::getHttpServletRequest).orElse(null));
343      var rn = McpRoutingNames.routingName(method, params);
344      var name = isEmpty(rn) ? null : rn;
345      var rawParams = params instanceof Map<?,?> m ? castParams(m) : Map.<String,Object>of();
346      McpResourceServerSupport.enforceOperationScopes(cfg, granted, new McpOperationContext(method, name, rawParams));
347   }
348
349   @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
350   private static Map<String,Object> castParams(Map<?,?> m) {
351      return (Map<String,Object>)m;
352   }

354   /**
355    * Capability-gates, limit-checks, registers, and constructs the streaming publisher for {@code
356    * subscriptions/listen}. Bypasses {@link #finalizeResult} / {@link JsonRpcResponse#ok}: the successful
357    * result is a {@code Flow.Publisher<SseEvent>}, not a JSON-RPC envelope. A thrown {@link McpException}
358    * (for example the over-limit case) is caught by {@link #dispatch}'s existing {@code McpException}
359    * handler, which builds the normal JSON-RPC error envelope.
360    *
361    * @param exchange The transport-neutral request/header accessor, used to enforce the SSE {@code Accept}
362    *    gate below before any broker registration happens.
363    * @param id The JSON-RPC request id. Never <jk>null</jk> (this method is never called for a notification).
364    * @param params The opaque request params. Must decode to a {@code SubscriptionsListenRequest}.
365    * @param config The neutral handler registry, used to auto-derive capabilities when none were set explicitly.
366    * @param ctx The per-request bean store, expected to carry a bound {@link McpSubscriptionBroker}
367    *    (Phase 1-3 wiring) and a bound {@link McpOptions}. In production the options bean is normally present —
368    *    {@code McpRestServlet#getMcpOptions()} / {@code McpEndpoint#mcpOptionsBean()} publish it into
369    *    the {@code RestContext} bean store that this request-scoped {@code ctx} wraps as its parent, since the
370    *    neutral core cannot add it directly ({@code McpOptions} is a v2 type). The
371    *    {@code orElseGet(McpSubscriptionsConfig::new)} fallback below is defense-in-depth only (e.g. a
372    *    hand-built {@code ctx} in a direct-dispatch test that omits it).
373    * <p>
374    * <b>SSE negotiation gate (checked first, before any broker registration):</b> every MCP servlet binding
375    * defaults an unqualified request to {@code Accept: application/json}. A {@code subscriptions/listen}
376    * call that never negotiated {@code text/event-stream} would still register with the broker and hand
377    * back a real {@code Flow.Publisher}, but {@code ReactiveResponseProcessor} would then render it in its
378    * BUFFER shape (unbounded {@code request(Long.MAX_VALUE)} demand, collected into a list that is only
379    * flushed once the publisher completes — which, for a live subscription, is never, until the connection
380    * itself drops). Because this dead-client cleanup is write-failure-driven (see the class javadoc), a
381    * BUFFER-shape stream never even attempts a write, so the broker slot, the pump thread, and the
382    * heartbeat executor all leak permanently, and any caller can trigger this for free. Checking {@code
383    * exchange.header("Accept")} here, before {@link McpSubscriptionBroker#registerIfUnder} is ever called,
384    * closes that hole at zero cost to a well-behaved caller (see {@code McpClient#listen} /
385    * {@code AbstractMcpClient#openEventStream}, which already always negotiate SSE on this call).
386    *
387    * <p>
388    * {@code maxConcurrentSubscriptions} is enforced as a hard cap, not an advisory one: the admission check
389    * and the registration are one atomic step via {@link McpSubscriptionBroker#registerIfUnder}, so
390    * concurrent {@code subscriptions/listen} calls against the same broker (e.g. a custom broker explicitly
391    * shared across multiple bindings via {@link McpOptions#setSubscriptionBroker}) cannot all observe room
392    * under the cap and all register, which a separate {@code activeCount()} check followed by a separate
393    * {@code register(...)} call would allow.
394    *
395    * <p>
396    * The broker registers under a fresh {@link UUID}, never under the client-supplied JSON-RPC request
397    * {@code id}: the broker's registry is process-wide (see {@link McpEndpoint#subscriptionBroker()}), so
398    * two unrelated concurrent listens that happen to share the same client id would otherwise evict each
399    * other's stream (the second {@code register(...)} call under a shared key closes whichever
400    * subscription is already registered there). The client's original {@code id} is passed to
401    * {@link SubscriptionsListenPublisher} unchanged and is still what every ack/notification frame on that
402    * client's own stream carries as its {@code _meta.subscriptionId} — this only decouples the *internal*
403    * registry key from the *wire* id, which stays exactly as the spec expects.
404    *
405    * @return The {@code Flow.Publisher<SseEvent>} for the newly registered subscription.
406    * @throws McpException If the caller never negotiated {@code text/event-stream}, the broker bean is
407    *    missing, or {@code maxConcurrentSubscriptions} is reached.
408    */
409   @SuppressWarnings({
410      "resource" // subscription's ownership transfers to the returned SubscriptionsListenPublisher, which closes it in every terminal path (cancel(), terminateWithError(), checkIdle(), run()'s completion - see its own @Owning-suppressed field). Eclipse JDT @Owning warning is by design; it surfaces at the return statement, so suppress at method scope.
411   })
412   private Flow.Publisher<SseEvent> dispatchSubscriptionsListen(McpExchange exchange, Object id, Object params, McpServerConfig config, BeanStore ctx) {
413      requireEventStreamAccept(exchange);
414      var request = Json.to(Json.of(params), SubscriptionsListenRequest.class);
415      var caps = discoverCapabilities(config);
416      var honoredFilter = SubscriptionCapabilityGate.honor(request.getNotifications(), caps);
417
418      var broker = ctx.getBean(McpSubscriptionBroker.class)
419         .orElseThrow(() -> new McpException(CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR, "McpSubscriptionBroker not bound in BeanStore"));
420      var subscriptionsConfig = ctx.getBean(McpOptions.class).map(McpOptions::getSubscriptions).orElseGet(McpSubscriptionsConfig::new);
421      // registerIfUnder admission-checks and registers as one atomic step (hard cap, not advisory) — a
422      // separate activeCount() check followed by a separate register() call would leave a TOCTOU window
423      // open for concurrent listen requests racing the same per-binding broker (see
424      // McpOptions#resolveSubscriptionBroker()). The registry key is a server-minted UUID, deliberately
425      // NOT String.valueOf(id): see the javadoc above.
426      var subscription = broker.registerIfUnder(subscriptionsConfig.getMaxConcurrentSubscriptions(), UUID.randomUUID().toString(), honoredFilter)
427         .orElseThrow(() -> new McpException(CODE_TOO_MANY_SUBSCRIPTIONS, "Maximum concurrent subscriptions exceeded"));
428      var honoredWireFilter = SubscriptionCapabilityGate.toWireFilter(honoredFilter);
429      return new SubscriptionsListenPublisher(id, honoredWireFilter, subscription, subscriptionsConfig.getHeartbeatIntervalMs(), subscriptionsConfig.getIdleTimeoutMs());
430   }
431
432   /**
433    * C1: rejects a {@code subscriptions/listen} call that never negotiated {@code text/event-stream},
434    * before any broker registration happens (see {@link #dispatchSubscriptionsListen}'s javadoc).
435    *
436    * <p>
437    * A bare {@code Accept: * / *} (every media type acceptable) is rejected exactly like an absent
438    * {@code Accept} header: this endpoint requires the caller to have explicitly negotiated
439    * {@code text/event-stream}, not merely to be willing to accept it among everything else. Without this,
440    * a wildcard-accepting request would fall into {@code ReactiveResponseProcessor}'s non-streaming BUFFER
441    * shape (the same permanent-leak hole C1 closes for a missing header), rather than the STREAM shape
442    * this method exists to require. A well-behaved caller is unaffected: both {@code McpClient#listen} and
443    * the underlying {@code AbstractMcpClient#openEventStream} already always send the explicit
444    * {@code text/event-stream} value on this call.
445    *
446    * @param exchange The transport-neutral request/header accessor. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
447    * @throws McpException If the {@code Accept} header is absent or does not contain {@code text/event-stream}
448    *    (case-insensitive, substring match — a real client's {@code Accept} header is commonly a
449    *    comma-separated list of media-type ranges, not the bare value alone).
450    */
451   private static void requireEventStreamAccept(McpExchange exchange) {
452      var accept = exchange.header("Accept");
453      if (accept == null || ! accept.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).contains("text/event-stream"))
454         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_REQUEST, "subscriptions/listen requires Accept: text/event-stream");
455   }
456
457   /**
458    * Builds a JSON-RPC error response, first giving an active request-scoped tracing observation a
459    * chance to record the outcome via {@link #recordRpcError(BeanStore, int, String)} &mdash; every
460    * dated dispatch returns JSON-RPC errors over HTTP {@code 200}, so this is the only place such an
461    * outcome reaches an active span.
462    *
463    * @param ctx The request-scoped bean store. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
464    * @param id The JSON-RPC request id, or <jk>null</jk> when the envelope itself could not be read.
465    * @param code The JSON-RPC error code.
466    * @param message The JSON-RPC error message.
467    * @return The error response. Never <jk>null</jk>.
468    */
469   private static JsonRpcResponse reportError(BeanStore ctx, Object id, int code, String message) {
470      recordRpcError(ctx, code, message);
471      return JsonRpcResponse.errorResponse(id, code, message);
472   }
473
474   /**
475    * Records a JSON-RPC error outcome on the active request-scoped {@link Scope}, if any.
476    *
477    * <p>
478    * A neutral no-op &mdash; no OpenTelemetry import involved &mdash; when no tracer is active for
479    * this request (no {@link Scope} was stashed under {@link TraceContextResponseProcessor#ATTR_SCOPE}
480    * by {@code RestOpInvoker}) or when the request-scoped {@link RestRequest} itself is unavailable
481    * (for example, a unit test dispatching directly against a bare {@link BeanStore}).
482    *
483    * @param ctx The request-scoped bean store. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
484    * @param code The JSON-RPC error code.
485    * @param message The JSON-RPC error message.
486    */
487   @SuppressWarnings({
488      "resource" // scope is owned/closed by RestOpInvoker's finally block after the handler returns; reading it here must not close it early.
489   })
490   private static void recordRpcError(BeanStore ctx, int code, String message) {
491      ctx.getBean(RestRequest.class).ifPresent(request -> {
492         var scope = request.getAttribute(TraceContextResponseProcessor.ATTR_SCOPE).as(Scope.class).orElse(null);
493         if (scope != null)
494            scope.recordRpcError(code, message);
495      });
496   }
497
498   // --- SEP-2243 header/body agreement -----------------------------------------------------
499
500   private static void validateHeaders(McpExchange exchange, JsonRpcRequest req) {
501      var headerMethod = exchange.header("Mcp-Method");
502      if (headerMethod == null)
503         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_REQUEST, "Missing required header: Mcp-Method");
504      var headerName = exchange.header("Mcp-Name");
505      if (headerName == null)
506         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_REQUEST, "Missing required header: Mcp-Name");
507      var method = req.getMethod();
508      if (! headerMethod.equals(method))
509         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_REQUEST, "Mcp-Method header '" + headerMethod + "' does not match request method '" + method + "'");
510      var name = McpRoutingNames.routingName(method, req.getParams());
511      if (! headerName.equals(name))
512         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_REQUEST, "Mcp-Name header '" + headerName + "' does not match request name '" + name + "'");
513   }
514
515   // --- per-request params._meta negotiation -----------------------------------------------
516
517   /**
518    * Validates the opaque {@code params._meta} shape directly.
519    *
520    * <p>
521    * The parsed {@link RequestMeta} bean cannot distinguish a malformed {@code clientCapabilities} (a
522    * scalar/array) from an absent one — parsing either into {@code ClientCapabilities} raises a
523    * generic parse error rather than a validation failure — so metadata shape is checked against
524    * the opaque map to produce the exact per-field {@code -32600} messages naming the exact wire path.
525    *
526    * @param params The opaque request params (the JSON-RPC {@code params} member). Can be <jk>null</jk>.
527    */
528   private static void validateMeta(Object params) {
529      if (! (params instanceof Map<?,?> p))
530         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_REQUEST, "Request params must be an object");
531      var meta = p.get(META_KEY);
532      if (! (meta instanceof Map<?,?> m))
533         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_REQUEST, "Request params._meta must be an object");
534      var protocolVersion = str(m.get(RequestMeta.KEY_PROTOCOL_VERSION));
535      if (isEmpty(protocolVersion))
536         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_REQUEST, "Missing required params._meta." + RequestMeta.KEY_PROTOCOL_VERSION);
537      if (! McpProtocol.VERSION_2026_07_28.equals(protocolVersion))
538         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_REQUEST, "Unsupported protocol version: " + protocolVersion);
539      var clientInfo = m.get(RequestMeta.KEY_CLIENT_INFO);
540      if (clientInfo != null && (! (clientInfo instanceof Map<?,?> ci) || isEmpty(str(ci.get("name"))) || isEmpty(str(ci.get("version")))))
541         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_REQUEST, "Malformed params._meta." + RequestMeta.KEY_CLIENT_INFO);
542      if (! m.containsKey(RequestMeta.KEY_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES) || m.get(RequestMeta.KEY_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES) == null)
543         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_REQUEST, "Missing required params._meta." + RequestMeta.KEY_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES);
544      if (! (m.get(RequestMeta.KEY_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES) instanceof Map<?,?>))
545         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_REQUEST, "params._meta." + RequestMeta.KEY_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES + " must be an object");
546   }
547
548   private static String str(Object value) {
549      return value == null ? null : value.toString();
550   }
551
552   /**
553    * Attaches the common success-result finalization to every dispatched result: a {@code "complete"}
554    * {@code resultType} (already the {@link Result} default) and {@link ResultMeta#getServerInfo() server
555    * identity} under {@code _meta}, without disturbing cache hints or payload fields a method already set.
556    *
557    * @param result The neutral-to-wire result returned by {@link #invoke}. Can be any wire result type.
558    * @param config The server configuration supplying server identity.
559    * @return The same {@code result} instance, finalized in place.
560    */
561   private static Object finalizeResult(Object result, McpServerConfig config, BeanStore ctx) {
562      if (result instanceof Result<?> r) {
563         var meta = r.getMeta();
564         if (meta == null)
565            meta = new ResultMeta();
566         meta.setServerInfo(McpWire.serverInfo(config));
567         echoTraceContext(meta, ctx);
568         r.setMeta(meta);
569      }
570      return result;
571   }
572
573   /**
574    * Echoes the request-scoped W3C trace context into a successful result's {@code _meta}.
575    *
576    * <p>
577    * At span-start time, an active {@code TracerHook} bridge (for example {@code OtelTracerHook})
578    * stashes the rendered {@code traceparent} / {@code tracestate} / {@code baggage} values as
579    * {@link RestRequest} attributes under {@link TraceContextResponseProcessor#ATTR_TRACEPARENT} /
580    * {@code ATTR_TRACESTATE} / {@code ATTR_BAGGAGE}. This copies those same values &mdash; already
581    * neutral strings, read here with no OpenTelemetry import &mdash; into <c>meta</c> so a caller can
582    * read the server-started trace identifiers off the JSON-RPC result body, in addition to the HTTP
583    * response headers {@link TraceContextResponseProcessor} emits from the same captured values.
584    *
585    * <p>
586    * A no-op &mdash; no trace keys added &mdash; when no tracer is active (no {@code ATTR_TRACEPARENT}
587    * was stashed) or when the request-scoped {@link RestRequest} itself is unavailable.
588    *
589    * @param meta The result metadata to enrich in place. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
590    * @param ctx The request-scoped bean store. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
591    */
592   private static void echoTraceContext(ResultMeta meta, BeanStore ctx) {
593      ctx.getBean(RestRequest.class).ifPresent(request -> {
594         var traceparent = request.getAttribute(TraceContextResponseProcessor.ATTR_TRACEPARENT).as(String.class).orElse(null);
595         if (isEmpty(traceparent))
596            return;
597         meta.setTraceparent(traceparent);
598         var tracestate = request.getAttribute(TraceContextResponseProcessor.ATTR_TRACESTATE).as(String.class).orElse(null);
599         if (! isEmpty(tracestate))
600            meta.setTracestate(tracestate);
601         var baggage = request.getAttribute(TraceContextResponseProcessor.ATTR_BAGGAGE).as(String.class).orElse(null);
602         if (! isEmpty(baggage))
603            meta.setBaggage(baggage);
604      });
605   }
606
607   // --- method table -----------------------------------------------------------------------
608
609   private Object invoke(String method, Object params, McpServerConfig config, BeanStore ctx) {
610      return switch (method) {
611         case McpMethods.SERVER_DISCOVER -> discover(config);
612         case McpMethods.PING -> new PingResult();
613         case McpMethods.TOOLS_LIST -> listTools(config, params, ctx);
614         case McpMethods.TOOLS_CALL -> callTool(config, params, ctx);
615         case McpMethods.PROMPTS_LIST -> listPrompts(config, params, ctx);
616         case McpMethods.PROMPTS_GET -> getPrompt(config, params, ctx);
617         case McpMethods.RESOURCES_LIST -> listResources(config, params, ctx);
618         case McpMethods.RESOURCES_READ -> readResource(config, params, ctx);
619         case McpMethods.RESOURCES_TEMPLATES_LIST -> listResourceTemplates(config, params, ctx);
620         case McpMethods.COMPLETION_COMPLETE -> complete(config, params, ctx);
621         default -> throw new McpException(errorCode(McpErrorKind.UNKNOWN_METHOD), "Method not found: " + method);
622      };
623   }
624
625   // --- cache-hint precedence ---------------------------------------------------------------
626
627   private static McpCacheHint first(McpCacheHint... values) {
628      for (var value : values)
629         if (value != null)
630            return value;
631      return null;
632   }
633
634   private static <T extends CacheableResult<T>> T applyCache(T result, McpCacheHint hint) {
635      if (hint != null) {
636         result.setTtlMs(hint.getTtlMs());
637         result.setCacheScope(hint.getCacheScope());
638      }
639      return result;
640   }
641
642   private McpCacheHint readHint(String uri) {
643      return first(cacheConfig.getResourceReadOverrides().get(uri),
644         cacheConfig.getResourcesRead(), cacheConfig.getDefaultHint());
645   }
646
647   private ServerDiscoverResult discover(McpServerConfig config) {
648      var result = McpWire.discover(discoverCapabilities(config), protocolVersion(), instructions);
649      return applyCache(result, first(cacheConfig.getServerDiscover(), cacheConfig.getDefaultHint()));
650   }
651
652   private ServerCapabilities discoverCapabilities(McpServerConfig config) {
653      var caps = this.capabilities;
654      if (caps == null) {
655         caps = new ServerCapabilities();
656         if (! config.getTools().isEmpty())
657            caps.setTools(new ToolCapability());
658         if (! config.getPrompts().isEmpty())
659            caps.setPrompts(new PromptCapability());
660         if (! config.getResources().isEmpty() || ! config.getResourceTemplates().isEmpty())
661            caps.setResources(new ResourceCapability());
662         if (config.hasAnyCompleter())
663            caps.setCompletions(new CompletionCapability());
664      }
665      return caps;
666   }
667
668   private ListToolsResult listTools(McpServerConfig config, Object params, BeanStore ctx) {
669      var descriptors = config.getTools().stream().map(McpToolHandler::descriptor).toList();
670      var page = config.getCursor().page(descriptors, McpCursor.cursorOf(params), ctx);
671      return applyCache(new ListToolsResult()
672         .setTools(page.items().stream().map(McpWire::toWire).toList())
673         .setNextCursor(page.nextCursor()),
674         first(cacheConfig.getToolsList(), cacheConfig.getDefaultHint()));
675   }
676
677   private Object callTool(McpServerConfig config, Object params, BeanStore ctx) {
678      var p = McpParamUtils.asMap(params);
679      var name = McpParamUtils.strParam(p, "name");
680      if (name == null)
681         throw new McpException(errorCode(McpErrorKind.INVALID_PARAMS), "Missing tool name");
682      var handler = config.getTools().stream()
683         .filter(h -> name.equals(h.descriptor().getName()))
684         .findFirst()
685         .orElseThrow(() -> new McpException(errorCode(McpErrorKind.TOOL_NOT_FOUND), "Tool not found: " + name));
686      var args = McpParamUtils.mapParam(p, PARAM_ARGUMENTS);
687      McpSchemaSafety.validateInput(handler.descriptor().getInputSchema(), args);
688      var mrtr = resolveMrtrContext(McpMethods.TOOLS_CALL, p, ctx);
689      try (var store = mrtr.store()) {
690         var outcome = handler.call(args, store);
691         validateStructuredOutput(outcome);
692         return McpWire.toWire(outcome);
693      } catch (McpInputRequiredSignal signal) {
694         return pause(signal, McpMethods.TOOLS_CALL, p, mrtr.currentRound(), mrtr.argumentsHash(), mrtr.target(), ctx);
695      }
696   }
697
698   private static void validateStructuredOutput(McpToolOutcome outcome) {
699      if (outcome == null || outcome.getStructuredContent() == null)
700         return;
701      try {
702         JsonValueSafety.check(outcome.getStructuredContent(), "Tool structuredContent");
703      } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
704         throw new McpException(CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR, e.getMessage());
705      }
706   }
707
708   private ListPromptsResult listPrompts(McpServerConfig config, Object params, BeanStore ctx) {
709      var descriptors = config.getPrompts().stream().map(McpPromptHandler::descriptor).toList();
710      var page = config.getCursor().page(descriptors, McpCursor.cursorOf(params), ctx);
711      return applyCache(new ListPromptsResult()
712         .setPrompts(page.items().stream().map(McpWire::toWire).toList())
713         .setNextCursor(page.nextCursor()),
714         first(cacheConfig.getPromptsList(), cacheConfig.getDefaultHint()));
715   }
716
717   private Object getPrompt(McpServerConfig config, Object params, BeanStore ctx) {
718      var p = McpParamUtils.asMap(params);
719      var name = McpParamUtils.strParam(p, "name");
720      if (name == null)
721         throw new McpException(errorCode(McpErrorKind.INVALID_PARAMS), "Missing prompt name");
722      var handler = config.getPrompts().stream()
723         .filter(h -> name.equals(h.descriptor().getName()))
724         .findFirst()
725         .orElseThrow(() -> new McpException(errorCode(McpErrorKind.PROMPT_NOT_FOUND), "Prompt not found: " + name));
726      var args = McpParamUtils.mapParam(p, PARAM_ARGUMENTS);
727      var mrtr = resolveMrtrContext(McpMethods.PROMPTS_GET, p, ctx);
728      try (var store = mrtr.store()) {
729         return McpWire.toWire(handler.get(args, store));
730      } catch (McpInputRequiredSignal signal) {
731         return pause(signal, McpMethods.PROMPTS_GET, p, mrtr.currentRound(), mrtr.argumentsHash(), mrtr.target(), ctx);
732      }
733   }
734
735   private ListResourcesResult listResources(McpServerConfig config, Object params, BeanStore ctx) {
736      var descriptors = config.getResources().stream().map(McpResourceHandler::descriptor).toList();
737      var page = config.getCursor().page(descriptors, McpCursor.cursorOf(params), ctx);
738      return applyCache(new ListResourcesResult()
739         .setResources(page.items().stream().map(McpWire::toWire).toList())
740         .setNextCursor(page.nextCursor()),
741         first(cacheConfig.getResourcesList(), cacheConfig.getDefaultHint()));
742   }
743
744   private Object readResource(McpServerConfig config, Object params, BeanStore ctx) {
745      var p = McpParamUtils.asMap(params);
746      var uri = McpParamUtils.strParam(p, "uri");
747      if (uri == null)
748         throw new McpException(errorCode(McpErrorKind.INVALID_PARAMS), "Missing resource uri");
749      var exact = config.getResources().stream()
750         .filter(h -> uri.equals(h.descriptor().getUri()))
751         .findFirst();
752      if (exact.isPresent()) {
753         // MRTR PAUSE/RESUME applies only to the exact-resource path; C4's resource-template branch below is
754         // untouched (spec rule 5). A PAUSE returns before applyCache(...), so a pending result never gets a
755         // cache hint.
756         var mrtr = resolveMrtrContext(McpMethods.RESOURCES_READ, p, ctx);
757         try (var store = mrtr.store()) {
758            return applyCache(McpWire.toWire(exact.get().read(uri, store)), readHint(uri));
759         } catch (McpInputRequiredSignal signal) {
760            return pause(signal, McpMethods.RESOURCES_READ, p, mrtr.currentRound(), mrtr.argumentsHash(), mrtr.target(), ctx);
761         }
762      }
763      var match = config.resolveResourceTemplate(uri);
764      var outcome = match == null ? null : match.handler().read(uri, match.variables(), ctx);
765      if (outcome == null)
766         throw new McpException(errorCode(McpErrorKind.RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND), "Resource not found: " + uri);
767      return applyCache(McpWire.toWire(outcome), readHint(uri));
768   }
769
770   private ListResourceTemplatesResult listResourceTemplates(McpServerConfig config, Object params, BeanStore ctx) {
771      var descriptors = config.getResourceTemplates().stream().map(McpResourceTemplateHandler::descriptor).toList();
772      var page = config.getCursor().page(descriptors, McpCursor.cursorOf(params), ctx);
773      return applyCache(new ListResourceTemplatesResult()
774         .setResourceTemplates(page.items().stream().map(McpWire::toWire).toList())
775         .setNextCursor(page.nextCursor()),
776         first(cacheConfig.getResourceTemplatesList(), cacheConfig.getDefaultHint()));
777   }
778
779   private CompleteResult complete(McpServerConfig config, Object params, BeanStore ctx) {
780      var p = McpParamUtils.asMap(params);
781      var ref = completionRef(McpParamUtils.mapParam(p, "ref"));
782      var argument = McpParamUtils.mapParam(p, "argument");
783      var argumentName = McpParamUtils.strParam(argument, "name");
784      if (isEmpty(argumentName))
785         throw new McpException(errorCode(McpErrorKind.INVALID_PARAMS), "Missing argument.name");
786      var value = McpParamUtils.strictStrParam(argument, "value");
787      if (value == null)
788         throw new McpException(errorCode(McpErrorKind.INVALID_PARAMS), "Missing or non-string argument.value");
789      var contextArguments = McpParamUtils.strictStrMapParam(McpParamUtils.mapParam(p, "context"), PARAM_ARGUMENTS);
790
791      var completer = config.completer(ref, argumentName);
792      McpCompletionResult raw;
793      if (completer == null) {
794         raw = McpCompletionResult.empty();
795      } else {
796         var request = new McpCompletionRequest()
797            .setRef(ref)
798            .setArgumentName(argumentName)
799            .setValue(value)
800            .setContextArguments(contextArguments);
801         raw = completer.complete(request, ctx);
802      }
803      return McpWire.toWire(McpCompletionResult.normalize(raw));
804   }
805
806   private McpCompletionRef completionRef(Map<String,Object> refMap) {
807      var type = McpParamUtils.strParam(refMap, "type");
808      if ("ref/prompt".equals(type)) {
809         var name = McpParamUtils.strParam(refMap, "name");
810         if (isEmpty(name))
811            throw new McpException(errorCode(McpErrorKind.INVALID_PARAMS), "Missing ref.name for ref/prompt");
812         return McpCompletionRef.prompt(name);
813      }
814      if ("ref/resource".equals(type)) {
815         var uri = McpParamUtils.strParam(refMap, "uri");
816         if (isEmpty(uri))
817            throw new McpException(errorCode(McpErrorKind.INVALID_PARAMS), "Missing ref.uri for ref/resource");
818         return McpCompletionRef.resource(uri);
819      }
820      throw new McpException(errorCode(McpErrorKind.INVALID_PARAMS), "Invalid or missing ref.type: " + type);
821   }
822
823   // --- MRTR (Multi-Round-Trip Request) pause/resume ---------------------------------------
824
825   /**
826    * The per-request MRTR resolution result: the {@link WritableBeanStore} a handler is invoked with (always
827    * carrying {@link McpMrtrCapabilityContext}, and on a RESUME also {@link McpMrtrResumeContext}) plus the
828    * current round decoded from the echoed {@code requestState} (0 on a first-round call), threaded to
829    * {@link #pause} so it can increment without a second unseal.
830    *
831    * <p>
832    * {@code store} is typed {@link WritableBeanStore} (rather than the narrower {@link BeanStore}) specifically
833    * so call sites can close it in a try-with-resources block: any bean a handler resolves through it is tracked
834    * for {@code @PreDestroy} cleanup on <i>this</i> store, not the caller-owned {@code ctx} it wraps (see
835    * {@link BasicBeanStore#close()}), so it must be closed once the handler invocation completes.
836    *
837    * <p>
838    * {@code argumentsHash} is the canonical hash of the current request's {@code arguments} (see
839    * {@link #argumentsHash(Map)}), computed <i>once</i> here &mdash; before the handler runs &mdash; and threaded
840    * to {@link #pause} so the next token seals the hash of what the client actually sent, not a hash recomputed
841    * from the live {@code arguments} map after a handler may have mutated it in place.
842    *
843    * <p>
844    * {@code target} is the operation target resolved by {@link #mrtrTarget(String, Map)} (the tool/prompt
845    * {@code name} or resource {@code uri}), captured at the same pre-handler point as {@code argumentsHash} and
846    * for the same reason: {@link #pause} seals it into the next token's {@link #aad(String, String) AAD}
847    * unchanged, so a handler that mutates the live {@code params} map in place cannot shift which
848    * tool/prompt/resource the next token is bound to.
849    */
850   private record MrtrContext(WritableBeanStore store, int currentRound, String argumentsHash, String target) {}
851
852   /**
853    * Builds the {@link BeanStore} an in-scope handler receives and, on a RESUME, validates the echoed
854    * {@code requestState} before the handler runs.
855    *
856    * <p>
857    * Always wraps {@code ctx} with a {@link McpMrtrCapabilityContext} so a handler can pre-check the client's
858    * advertised {@code elicitation} capability (spec &sect;4). When the request carries a {@code requestState}
859    * (a RESUME), it is unsealed under the canonical AAD and validated for integrity, method agreement, expiry,
860    * the max-rounds cap, argument-hash agreement (always; see {@link #argumentsHash(Map)}), and replay (only when
861    * {@link McpMrtrConfig#getReplayCache()} is configured; see {@link #checkReplay(ReplayCache, String, long)})
862    * &mdash; any failure raises the mapped {@link McpException} <i>before</i> the handler is re-invoked &mdash;
863    * then the decoded continuation and the client's {@code inputResponses} are exposed via
864    * {@link McpMrtrResumeContext}.
865    *
866    * <p>
867    * <b>Check ordering is deliberate.</b> The stateless argument-hash comparison runs <i>before</i> the
868    * (stateful) replay {@code checkAndRecord}, so a submission carrying the wrong {@code arguments} is rejected
869    * without ever consuming the token's {@code jti} &mdash; an attacker holding only a leaked token (but not the
870    * arguments) cannot burn a victim's in-flight resume, and an honest client that sends slightly-wrong arguments
871    * does not destroy its own token. The argument hash is also computed <i>once</i> here, before the handler
872    * runs, and threaded to {@link #pause} (see {@link MrtrContext}).
873    *
874    * @param method The in-scope JSON-RPC method. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
875    * @param params The request params map. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
876    * @param ctx The request-scoped bean store to wrap. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
877    * @return The resolved MRTR context. Never <jk>null</jk>.
878    */
879   @SuppressWarnings({
880      "resource" // wrapped (both branches) is @Owning: ownership transfers to the returned MrtrContext, which the caller closes via mrtr.store() in try-with-resources (see MrtrContext's javadoc above). Eclipse JDT @Owning warning is by design; it surfaces at the two `return new MrtrContext(wrapped, ...)` statements, so suppress at method scope.
881   })
882   private MrtrContext resolveMrtrContext(String method, Map<String,Object> params, BeanStore ctx) {
883      // Computed once, up front, from the CURRENT request's arguments: reused both for the RESUME-time
884      // comparison below and (threaded through MrtrContext) for the hash pause(...) seals into the next token,
885      // so a handler that mutates the live arguments map in place cannot make the next token seal a hash the
886      // client can no longer reproduce. Also applies the bounded-traversal + canonicalization guards (see
887      // argumentsHash), so structurally-hostile arguments become a -32602 here on both first-round and RESUME.
888      var argumentsHash = argumentsHash(McpParamUtils.mapParam(params, PARAM_ARGUMENTS));
889      // Captured once, up front, alongside argumentsHash and for the same reason: threaded through MrtrContext
890      // to pause(...) so the AAD sealed into the next token binds the target actually resolved for THIS
891      // request, immune to a handler mutating params in place before pause(...) runs (see MrtrContext's
892      // javadoc above).
893      var target = mrtrTarget(method, params);
894      var requestState = McpParamUtils.strParam(params, "requestState");
895      if (requestState == null) {
896         var wrapped = new BasicBeanStore(ctx)
897            .addBean(McpMrtrCapabilityContext.class, new McpMrtrCapabilityContext(clientElicitationSupported(params)));
898         return new MrtrContext(wrapped, 0, argumentsHash, target);
899      }
900      // Validate the echoed requestState before constructing the BasicBeanStore below: every failure here
901      // throws, and a BasicBeanStore built earlier would never reach a caller's try-with-resources to be
902      // closed (java:S2095). Deferring construction until validation succeeds means no path leaks it.
903      var sealed = mrtrConfig.getCodec().unseal(requestState, aad(method, target), principal(ctx))
904         .orElseThrow(() -> new McpException(CODE_INVALID_PARAMS, "Invalid or tampered requestState"));
905      if (! method.equals(sealed.method()))
906         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_PARAMS, "requestState method mismatch");
907      if (sealed.expiresAtMs() <= System.currentTimeMillis())
908         throw new McpException(CODE_REQUEST_STATE_EXPIRED, "requestState has expired");
909      if (sealed.round() >= mrtrConfig.getMaxRounds())
910         // Client-facing message deliberately omits the configured cap value so server config is not leaked.
911         throw new McpException(CODE_MAX_ROUNDS_EXCEEDED, "Max MRTR rounds exceeded");
912      // Stateless argument-hash agreement BEFORE the stateful replay record (see the ordering note above). A
913      // null sealed hash (e.g. a custom codec that dropped the field) fails closed as an ordinary mismatch
914      // here; a malformed (non-base64url) sealed hash is a codec-contract violation and argumentsMatch itself
915      // throws CODE_INVALID_PARAMS for it (mirroring the null-jti fail-closed check below), rather than
916      // reaching this mismatch branch.
917      if (! argumentsMatch(argumentsHash, sealed.argumentsHash()))
918         throw new McpException(CODE_REQUEST_STATE_ARGUMENTS_MISMATCH, "resumed arguments do not match the original request");
919      var replayCache = mrtrConfig.getReplayCache();
920      if (replayCache != null) {
921         // A null/empty jti reaching the cache is a codec/contract violation (a custom RequestStateCodec that
922         // dropped the field, or a pre-jti in-flight token during a rolling deploy), NOT a store outage: fail
923         // CLOSED here rather than letting a downstream NPE be swallowed by checkReplay's fail-OPEN catch,
924         // which would silently disable replay protection.
925         if (isEmpty(sealed.jti()))
926            throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_PARAMS, "Invalid or tampered requestState");
927         if (! checkReplay(replayCache, sealed.jti(), sealed.expiresAtMs()))
928            // Client-facing message deliberately omits any cache/backend detail, mirroring the max-rounds
929            // message's "don't leak server config" caution above.
930            throw new McpException(CODE_REQUEST_STATE_REPLAYED, "requestState has already been used");
931      }
932      var inputResponses = McpParamUtils.mapParam(params, "inputResponses");
933      var wrapped = new BasicBeanStore(ctx)
934         .addBean(McpMrtrCapabilityContext.class, new McpMrtrCapabilityContext(clientElicitationSupported(params)))
935         .addBean(McpMrtrResumeContext.class, new McpMrtrResumeContext(sealed.continuation(), inputResponses));
936      return new MrtrContext(wrapped, sealed.round(), argumentsHash, target);
937   }
938
939   /**
940    * Turns a caught {@link McpInputRequiredSignal} into a wire {@link InputRequiredResult}: capability-gates the
941    * client, seals a fresh {@code requestState} carrying the incremented round counter, a fresh {@code jti} (see
942    * {@link #mintJti()}), and the {@code argumentsHash} of the current request's {@code arguments} (see
943    * {@link #argumentsHash(Map)}), and assembles the requested-inputs map.
944    *
945    * <p>
946    * The capability gate runs <i>before</i> any token is minted &mdash; a client that never advertised
947    * {@code elicitation} causes no seal at all, only a {@link #CODE_MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY} error.
948    *
949    * @param signal The signal thrown by the handler. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
950    * @param method The in-scope JSON-RPC method this pause is for. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
951    * @param params The request params map, used only for {@link #clientElicitationSupported(Map)} here &mdash;
952    *    the AAD's operation target is the caller-supplied {@code target}, below, not re-derived from this map.
953    * @param currentRound The round decoded on RESUME (0 on a first-round pause), incremented into the new token.
954    * @param argumentsHash The hash of the current request's {@code arguments}, computed by
955    *    {@link #resolveMrtrContext} <i>before</i> the handler ran and threaded here (see {@link MrtrContext}), so a
956    *    handler that mutated the live {@code arguments} map cannot make this token seal an unreproducible hash.
957    * @param target The operation target sealed into the next token's {@link #aad(String, String) AAD}, resolved
958    *    by {@link #resolveMrtrContext} <i>before</i> the handler ran and threaded here (see {@link MrtrContext}),
959    *    so a handler that mutated the live {@code params} map cannot shift which tool/prompt/resource the next
960    *    token is bound to.
961    * @param ctx The per-request bean store, used to resolve the authenticated {@link #principal(BeanStore)} threaded
962    *    into the codec's {@link RequestStateCodec#seal seal} (READY-312f F4). Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
963    * @return The assembled, validated {@code input_required} result. Never <jk>null</jk>.
964    */
965   private InputRequiredResult pause(McpInputRequiredSignal signal, String method, Map<String,Object> params, int currentRound, String argumentsHash, String target, BeanStore ctx) {
966      if (! clientElicitationSupported(params))
967         throw new McpException(CODE_MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY,
968            "Client does not advertise the elicitation capability required for input_required");
969      var state = new McpRequestState(signal.getContinuation(), method, currentRound + 1, System.currentTimeMillis() + mrtrConfig.getTtlMs(),
970         mintJti(), argumentsHash);
971      var result = new InputRequiredResult().setRequestState(mrtrConfig.getCodec().seal(state, aad(method, target), principal(ctx)));
972      // Each inputRequests value is carried to the wire byte-for-byte as a raw sub-request object (see
973      // McpInputRequiredSignal). The pinned schema models every value as an object; a non-map handler value is a
974      // programming error that surfaces (as a ClassCastException here) via dispatch's -32603 fail-safe.
975      signal.getInputRequests().forEach((id, raw) -> result.putInputRequest(id, new JsonMap((Map<?,?>) raw)));
976      result.validate();
977      return result;
978   }
979
980   /**
981    * The canonical MRTR AAD binding a sealed {@code requestState} to the request that produced it:
982    * {@code method + '\u0000' + protocolVersion + '\u0000' + target} (NUL-separated; see
983    * {@link RequestStateCodec}).
984    *
985    * <p>
986    * <b>The operation {@code target} is folded in so a token is bound to the specific tool/prompt/resource it
987    * paused against, not merely the method.</b> Without it, a token paused for tool A could be resumed against
988    * tool B (or resource {@code uri} A against {@code uri} B) &mdash; both are {@code tools/call} (or
989    * {@code resources/read}), so the method-only AAD verified identically. The {@code target} is the tool
990    * {@code name} for {@code tools/call}, the prompt {@code name} for {@code prompts/get}, and the {@code uri}
991    * for {@code resources/read} (see {@link #mrtrTarget(String, Map)}); a mismatch now fails the GCM tag check,
992    * surfacing as the existing "invalid or tampered requestState" {@link #CODE_INVALID_PARAMS}. Neither
993    * {@code method} nor {@code protocolVersion} can contain a NUL, and {@code target} is the terminal field, so
994    * the three-field NUL join is unambiguous (distinct {@code (method, version, target)} tuples never collide)
995    * &mdash; the same injectivity property the two-field form relied on, extended by one trailing field. The
996    * codec treats this whole string as one opaque AAD field, framing it against {@code keyId}/principal with its
997    * own length-prefixed join (see {@link AeadRequestStateCodec#lengthPrefixJoin}).
998    *
999    * @param method The in-scope JSON-RPC method. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
1000    * @param target The operation target (tool/prompt {@code name} or resource {@code uri}); coalesced to empty
1001    *    when <jk>null</jk> (only the three MRTR-wired methods reach here, and each has already validated its
1002    *    target as non-null at the call site).
1003    * @return The AAD string. Never <jk>null</jk>.
1004    */
1005   private String aad(String method, String target) {
1006      return method + '\u0000' + protocolVersion() + '\u0000' + ein(target);
1007   }
1008
1009   /**
1010    * Derives the operation target folded into the {@link #aad(String, String) AAD}: the tool {@code name} for
1011    * {@code tools/call}, the prompt {@code name} for {@code prompts/get}, and the resource {@code uri} for
1012    * {@code resources/read}. Any other method (none of which reach the MRTR pause/resume path) yields
1013    * <jk>null</jk>.
1014    *
1015    * @param method The in-scope JSON-RPC method. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
1016    * @param params The request params map. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
1017    * @return The operation target, or <jk>null</jk> for a non-MRTR method.
1018    */
1019   private static String mrtrTarget(String method, Map<String,Object> params) {
1020      return switch (method) {
1021         case McpMethods.TOOLS_CALL, McpMethods.PROMPTS_GET -> McpParamUtils.strParam(params, "name");
1022         case McpMethods.RESOURCES_READ -> McpParamUtils.strParam(params, "uri");
1023         default -> null;
1024      };
1025   }
1026
1027   /**
1028    * Mints a fresh, per-token random {@code jti} for a newly-sealed {@code requestState}, used only to detect
1029    * replay of this exact token (see {@link #checkReplay(ReplayCache, String, long)}).
1030    *
1031    * <p>
1032    * 16 random bytes, base64url-encoded &mdash; the same minting pattern {@link EphemeralKeyProvider} already
1033    * uses for its own {@code keyId}. Collision probability is negligible (128 bits of entropy) and, in any
1034    * case, is not a security property this identifier depends on: it rides inside the AEAD-sealed plaintext, so
1035    * a client can neither forge nor read it without first breaking the GCM tag.
1036    *
1037    * @return A fresh {@code jti}. Never <jk>null</jk>.
1038    */
1039   private static String mintJti() {
1040      var bytes = new byte[JTI_BYTES];
1041      JTI_RANDOM.nextBytes(bytes);
1042      return B64URL.encodeToString(bytes);
1043   }
1044
1045   /**
1046    * Computes the canonical hash of a request's {@code arguments}, sealed at PAUSE time and re-verified at
1047    * RESUME time (see {@code McpRequestState#argumentsHash()}).
1048    *
1049    * <p>
1050    * First runs the module's shared bounded-traversal guard ({@link JsonValueSafety#check(Object, String)}:
1051    * {@code MAX_DEPTH=64}, {@code MAX_NODES}, a traversal-time deadline) so structurally-hostile {@code arguments}
1052    * (excessive depth or node count &mdash; reachable via {@code prompts/get}, which has no other input-shape
1053    * guard, and schemaless {@code tools/call}) become a deterministic {@link #CODE_INVALID_PARAMS} rejection on
1054    * BOTH PAUSE and RESUME, rather than a silent hash collision (the JCS canonicalizer's inherited depth limit
1055    * would otherwise truncate over-depth nodes to {@code null}). It then canonicalizes {@code arguments} per RFC
1056    * 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme) using an <b>unbounded-depth</b> serializer (see {@link #JCS}), SHA-256s
1057    * the canonical UTF-8 bytes, and base64url-encodes the digest (mirroring {@link EphemeralKeyProvider}'s
1058    * existing {@code keyId} encoding convention). An absent or empty {@code arguments} map canonicalizes to the
1059    * empty JSON object {@code "{}"}, giving a single, consistent sentinel hash for calls that take no arguments
1060    * (for example {@code resources/read}'s exact-path branch), so PAUSE and RESUME agree even when there is
1061    * nothing to hash.
1062    *
1063    * <p>
1064    * By design, RFC 8785 canonical equivalences are treated as equal &mdash; for example {@code 1} and
1065    * {@code 1.0} canonicalize identically, so they hash the same and a resume switching between them is not a
1066    * mismatch. A canonicalization failure on a hostile-but-syntactically-legal value (a non-finite number such
1067    * as {@code 1e999}, a lone UTF-16 surrogate, or a {@code BigDecimal}/{@code BigInteger} outside IEEE-754
1068    * range) is mapped to {@link #CODE_INVALID_PARAMS} rather than surfacing as a generic internal error.
1069    *
1070    * <p>
1071    * Package-visible so tests can construct {@link McpRequestState} fixtures whose {@code argumentsHash} agrees
1072    * with a given (or absent) {@code arguments} map without duplicating this derivation.
1073    *
1074    * @param arguments The request's {@code arguments} map, as returned by
1075    *    {@code McpParamUtils.mapParam(params, "arguments")}. Never <jk>null</jk> (empty when absent).
1076    * @return The canonical hash. Never <jk>null</jk>.
1077    * @throws McpException ({@link #CODE_INVALID_PARAMS}) if {@code arguments} violates the structural safety
1078    *    limits or cannot be canonicalized.
1079    */
1080   static String argumentsHash(Map<String,Object> arguments) {
1081      try {
1082         JsonValueSafety.check(arguments, PARAM_ARGUMENTS);
1083      } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
1084         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_PARAMS, e.getMessage());
1085      }
1086      String canonical;
1087      try {
1088         canonical = JCS.write(arguments);
1089      } catch (SerializeException e) {
1090         // Message deliberately generic (no echo of the offending value), mirroring the other MRTR "don't leak"
1091         // messages: a hostile-but-legal input (non-finite number, lone surrogate, out-of-IEEE BigDecimal) must
1092         // not surface as a -32603 internal error.
1093         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_PARAMS, "Invalid arguments: not canonicalizable");
1094      }
1095      return B64URL.encodeToString(sha256(canonical.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)));
1096   }
1097
1098   /**
1099    * Constant-time comparison of the current request's {@code argumentsHash} against the one sealed into the
1100    * echoed token. Both operands are base64url of a SHA-256 digest; they are decoded to their raw digest bytes
1101    * and compared with {@link MessageDigest#isEqual(byte[], byte[])}. A <jk>null</jk> sealed hash (for example a
1102    * custom codec that dropped the field) fails closed (returns <jk>false</jk>, surfacing as the ordinary
1103    * {@link #CODE_REQUEST_STATE_ARGUMENTS_MISMATCH} at the call site).
1104    *
1105    * <p>
1106    * A non-<jk>null</jk> sealed hash that is not valid base64url (for example a custom codec that computed
1107    * {@code argumentsHash} some other way) is a codec-contract violation rather than an ordinary mismatch, and
1108    * fails closed the same way the null-{@code jti} codec-contract violation does at the call site: a thrown
1109    * {@link McpException} ({@link #CODE_INVALID_PARAMS}), not a propagated {@link IllegalArgumentException}
1110    * from {@link Base64.Decoder#decode(String)} surfacing as a generic {@link #CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR}.
1111    *
1112    * @param currentHash The hash recomputed from the current request's {@code arguments}. Never <jk>null</jk>.
1113    * @param sealedHash The hash sealed into the echoed token, or <jk>null</jk>.
1114    * @return <jk>true</jk> if the two hashes match.
1115    * @throws McpException ({@link #CODE_INVALID_PARAMS}) if {@code sealedHash} is non-<jk>null</jk> but not
1116    *    valid base64url.
1117    */
1118   private static boolean argumentsMatch(String currentHash, String sealedHash) {
1119      if (sealedHash == null)
1120         return false;
1121      byte[] sealedBytes;
1122      try {
1123         sealedBytes = B64URL_DECODER.decode(sealedHash);
1124      } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
1125         // Same fail-closed contract as the null-jti check below: an untrusted or misbehaving codec must
1126         // never turn into a raw exception bubbling up as -32603 (see resolveMrtrContext's ordering note
1127         // on why this stateless check runs before the stateful replay record).
1128         throw new McpException(CODE_INVALID_PARAMS, "Invalid or tampered requestState");
1129      }
1130      return MessageDigest.isEqual(B64URL_DECODER.decode(currentHash), sealedBytes);
1131   }
1132
1133   private static byte[] sha256(byte[] input) {
1134      try {
1135         return MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256").digest(input);
1136      } catch (NoSuchAlgorithmException e) { // HTT every JDK guarantees SHA-256 via the standard JCE provider
1137         throw rex(e, "SHA-256 not available");
1138      }
1139   }
1140
1141   /**
1142    * Invokes an operator-configured {@link ReplayCache}, applying the fail-open policy documented on that SPI:
1143    * a thrown exception is logged and treated as first-seen, so a store outage degrades to today's
1144    * already-documented multi-use-tolerant behavior rather than rejecting all MRTR resume traffic.
1145    *
1146    * <p>
1147    * An operator who wants fail-closed-on-store-outage instead must implement that themselves by returning
1148    * <jk>false</jk> from their own {@link ReplayCache#checkAndRecord(String, long)} rather than throwing (see
1149    * the SPI's own Javadoc) &mdash; this method applies no policy beyond "don't let an unexpected exception take
1150    * down resume traffic".
1151    *
1152    * @param replayCache The configured replay cache. Must not be <jk>null</jk> (callers only invoke this when
1153    *    {@link McpMrtrConfig#getReplayCache()} is non-<jk>null</jk>).
1154    * @param jti The token identifier to check. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
1155    * @param expiresAtMs The sealed token's own absolute expiry, passed through unchanged.
1156    * @return <jk>true</jk> if the cache reports first-seen (or itself failed, fail-open); <jk>false</jk> only
1157    *    when the cache affirmatively reports a replay.
1158    */
1159   private static boolean checkReplay(ReplayCache replayCache, String jti, long expiresAtMs) {
1160      // MCP deliberately opts into fail-open: a thrown failure is logged and treated as first-seen, degrading a
1161      // transient store outage to the same multi-use-tolerant behavior seen when no ReplayCache is wired at all.
1162      return replayCache.checkAndRecord(jti, expiresAtMs, ReplayCache.FailMode.FAIL_OPEN,
1163         e -> LOG.log(Level.WARNING, e, () -> "ReplayCache.checkAndRecord failed; treating requestState as first-seen (fail-open)."));
1164   }
1165
1166   /**
1167    * Resolves the authenticated caller {@link Principal} for the current request, threaded into the
1168    * {@link RequestStateCodec} at seal and unseal so a hardened codec can bind the {@code requestState} to who
1169    * requested it (READY-312f F4; enables principal-bound AAD).
1170    *
1171    * <p>
1172    * Reads the F2 resource-server principal via {@link McpResourceServerSupport#principal} &mdash; the same
1173    * {@code RestRequest -> HttpServletRequest} lookup {@link #enforceStepUpScopes} uses for granted scopes, so the
1174    * two stay in lock-step. Returns <jk>null</jk> when there is no bound {@link RestRequest} (a direct-dispatch unit
1175    * test), when RS auth is disabled, or when the caller is anonymous &mdash; the codec must seal/unseal cleanly in
1176    * that case.
1177    *
1178    * @param ctx The per-request bean store. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
1179    * @return The authenticated principal, or <jk>null</jk> when none is available.
1180    */
1181   private static Principal principal(BeanStore ctx) {
1182      return ctx.getBean(RestRequest.class)
1183         .map(RestRequest::getHttpServletRequest)
1184         .map(McpResourceServerSupport::principal)
1185         .orElse(null);
1186   }
1187
1188   /**
1189    * Reads whether the request advertised the client {@code elicitation} capability, from the opaque
1190    * {@code _meta.clientCapabilities} map directly (mirroring {@link #validateMeta}'s opaque-map style rather than
1191    * re-parsing a full {@code RequestMeta}/{@code ClientCapabilities} bean for one key).
1192    *
1193    * @param params The request params map. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
1194    * <p>
1195    * {@link #validateMeta} has already run for every dispatched request and rejects a missing or non-{@code Map}
1196    * {@code clientCapabilities} with {@link #CODE_INVALID_REQUEST}, so {@code caps} is always a non-<jk>null</jk>
1197    * {@code Map} here &mdash; no defensive type guard is needed.
1198    *
1199    * @return <jk>true</jk> if {@code _meta.clientCapabilities.elicitation} is present and non-<jk>null</jk>.
1200    */
1201   private static boolean clientElicitationSupported(Map<String,Object> params) {
1202      var caps = (Map<?,?>) McpWire.metaMapOrEmpty(params).get(RequestMeta.KEY_CLIENT_CAPABILITIES);
1203      return caps.get("elicitation") != null;
1204   }
1205
1206   // --- trace-context extraction (Part B / trace-context propagation) ----------------------
1207
1208   /**
1209    * This revision's stable, stateless {@link TraceContextExtractor}, published as a {@code @Bean} by
1210    * both {@link McpRestServlet} and {@link McpEndpoint} so an active {@code TracerHook} can recognize
1211    * this revision's resolved {@link JsonRpcRequest} argument and its {@code params._meta} carrier
1212    * before span creation.
1213    *
1214    * <p>
1215    * Imports only the neutral {@code juneau-rest-server} tracing seam ({@link TraceContextExtractor},
1216    * {@link TraceContextCarrier}, {@link TraceOperation}) &mdash; never OpenTelemetry.
1217    */
1218   static final TraceContextExtractor TRACE_CONTEXT_EXTRACTOR = new V2TraceContextExtractor();
1219
1220   /**
1221    * {@link TraceContextExtractor} implementation for revision {@code 2026-07-28}.
1222    *
1223    * <p>
1224    * Recognizes the resolved {@link JsonRpcRequest} among {@code @RestOp}-resolved arguments, reads
1225    * its opaque {@code params._meta} (via {@link McpWire#metaMapOrEmpty(Object)}, since extraction
1226    * runs before {@link #validateMeta(Object)} enforces the per-request contract on a request that
1227    * has not yet been validated), and derives a composite carrier plus a low-cardinality
1228    * {@link TraceOperation}.
1229    */
1230   private static final class V2TraceContextExtractor implements TraceContextExtractor {
1231
1232      @Override /* TraceContextExtractor */
1233      public Optional<TraceContextCarrier> extract(RestRequest request, Object[] resolvedArguments) {
1234         var req = findRequest(resolvedArguments);
1235         if (req == null)
1236            return Optional.empty();
1237         var meta = new LinkedHashMap<>(McpWire.metaMapOrEmpty(req.getParams()));
1238         return Optional.of(new MetaCarrier(meta, request));
1239      }
1240
1241      @Override /* TraceContextExtractor */
1242      public TraceOperation operation(RestRequest request, Object[] resolvedArguments) {
1243         var req = findRequest(resolvedArguments);
1244         return req == null ? TraceOperation.DEFAULT : buildOperation(req);
1245      }
1246
1247      private static JsonRpcRequest findRequest(Object[] resolvedArguments) {
1248         for (var arg : resolvedArguments)
1249            if (arg instanceof JsonRpcRequest r)
1250               return r;
1251         return null;
1252      }
1253
1254      /**
1255       * Derives method, protocol version, request id, and tool/prompt/resource target into a
1256       * {@link TraceOperation}, following the exact pinned MCP/GenAI attribute and span-name mapping:
1257       * {@code "tools/call "+name}, {@code "prompts/get "+name}, bare {@code "resources/read"} (the
1258       * URI stays an attribute, never a span-name suffix), or the exact method name otherwise.
1259       */
1260      private static TraceOperation buildOperation(JsonRpcRequest req) {
1261         var method = req.getMethod();
1262         if (isEmpty(method))
1263            return TraceOperation.DEFAULT;
1264         var meta = McpWire.metaMapOrEmpty(req.getParams());
1265         var attrs = new LinkedHashMap<String,String>();
1266         attrs.put(TraceOperation.ATTR_MCP_METHOD_NAME, method);
1267         var protocolVersion = str(meta.get(RequestMeta.KEY_PROTOCOL_VERSION));
1268         if (! isEmpty(protocolVersion))
1269            attrs.put(TraceOperation.ATTR_MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION, protocolVersion);
1270         if (nn(req.getId()))
1271            attrs.put(TraceOperation.ATTR_JSONRPC_REQUEST_ID, String.valueOf(req.getId()));
1272
1273         var spanName = method;
1274         switch (method) {
1275            case McpMethods.TOOLS_CALL -> {
1276               var name = McpRoutingNames.routingName(method, req.getParams());
1277               if (! isEmpty(name)) {
1278                  attrs.put(TraceOperation.ATTR_GEN_AI_TOOL_NAME, name);
1279                  spanName = method + " " + name;
1280               }
1281               attrs.put(TraceOperation.ATTR_GEN_AI_OPERATION_NAME, "execute_tool");
1282            }
1283            case McpMethods.PROMPTS_GET -> {
1284               var name = McpRoutingNames.routingName(method, req.getParams());
1285               if (! isEmpty(name)) {
1286                  attrs.put(TraceOperation.ATTR_GEN_AI_PROMPT_NAME, name);
1287                  spanName = method + " " + name;
1288               }
1289            }
1290            case McpMethods.RESOURCES_READ -> {
1291               var uri = McpRoutingNames.routingName(method, req.getParams());
1292               if (! isEmpty(uri))
1293                  attrs.put(TraceOperation.ATTR_MCP_RESOURCE_URI, uri);
1294            }
1295            default -> {
1296               // Exact method name; no method-specific attributes.
1297            }
1298         }
1299         return TraceOperation.of(spanName, attrs);
1300      }
1301   }
1302
1303   /**
1304    * Composite, per-request {@link TraceContextCarrier} giving an explicit {@code params._meta} value
1305    * precedence over the equivalent HTTP header, for any key &mdash; in practice the bare W3C
1306    * {@code traceparent} / {@code tracestate} / {@code baggage} keys, since those are the only names
1307    * both sides share: {@code lookup(key) = params._meta[key] if present, otherwise the HTTP header of
1308    * the same name}.
1309    */
1310   private static final class MetaCarrier implements TraceContextCarrier {
1311      private final Map<String,Object> meta;
1312      private final RestRequest request;
1313
1314      MetaCarrier(Map<String,Object> meta, RestRequest request) {
1315         this.meta = meta;
1316         this.request = request;
1317      }
1318
1319      @Override /* TraceContextCarrier */
1320      public String get(String key) {
1321         var value = meta.get(key);
1322         if (nn(value))
1323            return value.toString();
1324         return request.getHeaderParam(key).orElse(null);
1325      }

1327      @Override /* TraceContextCarrier */
